candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether heavy rare-earth separation and 10X magnet capacity milestones are met on schedule, and whether commercial customers beyond government-linked offtake absorb volumes at economic margins.
candidates.next_evidence: Track SEC filings and company updates for 10X facility commissioning, heavy rare-earth separation expansion, NdPr price-floor payments, magnet offtake details, capex overruns, and customer mix.
candidates.node_relation: Reference domestic rare-earth supply-chain anchor with Mountain Pass rare-earth operations, heavy rare-earth separation expansion plans, and downstream NdFeB magnet manufacturing buildout.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth mining, separation, refining, and permanent magnets
candidates.theme_relation: Direct exposure to Western policy support, defense stockpiling, price-floor mechanisms, and non-Chinese rare-earth magnet supply-chain localization.
candidates.why_include: Included as the obvious public benchmark for US rare-earth processing and magnet independence. Its DoD partnership gives a concrete reference point for how policy support can translate into price floors, offtake, loans, and capacity buildout.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a context anchor so smaller processors and second-order beneficiaries can be compared against the leading public rare-earth name.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Confirm whether the hydrometallurgical demonstration facility produces heavy rare-earth oxide on the stated timeline and whether Round Top, Less Common Metals, Serra Verde, and magnet assets integrate into a bankable operating chain.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify CHIPS/Commerce funding closing conditions, PIPE proceeds use, Round Top consolidation, demonstration facility output, metallurgical recoveries, customer qualifications, and audited capex/ramp disclosures.
candidates.node_relation: Emerging vertically integrated rare-earth processor and magnet-chain company tied to Round Top, heavy rare-earth oxide demonstration work, and mine-to-magnet strategy.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Rare earth mining, hydrometallurgical processing, metals/alloys, and magnets
candidates.theme_relation: Potential beneficiary of export-control shocks and US industrial-policy funding aimed at building domestic rare-earth processing and magnet capacity.
candidates.why_include: USAR is more directly aligned with the node than diversified miners because the story centers on processing, heavy rare-earth oxides, and magnet-chain integration rather than only ore extraction.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Despite a multi-billion-dollar market cap, it is less institutionalized than MP and still has project-ramp, funding-close, metallurgy, and customer-qualification uncertainty that can keep analyst mindshare uneven.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether announced government funding and defense/customer demand convert into sustained revenue, margin expansion, domestic feedstock security, and non-dilutive capacity expansion rather than one-off headline effects.
candidates.next_evidence: Check DPA/DoD award documents, DLA or defense-contract details, smelter throughput, domestic feedstock acquisitions, customer concentration, working-capital needs, dilution risk, environmental compliance, and realized antimony prices.
candidates.node_relation: US-listed antimony processor with smelting and finished antimony-products exposure; positioned around domestic defense and critical-minerals supply-chain expansion.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Antimony processing, smelting, zeolite, and critical minerals
candidates.theme_relation: Directly tied to antimony scarcity, defense munitions demand, stockpiling, and policy attempts to reduce reliance on Chinese or foreign antimony supply.
candidates.why_include: Antimony is one of the cleaner chokepoint fits in this node because processing capacity is scarce, defense demand is strategic, and UAMY has public disclosures around processing and supply-chain expansion.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is obscure relative to rare-earth leaders and AI/defense primes; it sits several steps upstream of visible defense electronics and munitions demand, and its legacy micro/small-cap profile may have limited historical institutional coverage.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Kellyton secures replacement or durable offtake after reported customer terminations, obtains enough capital to complete Phase I, and proves commercial-scale CSPG quality and cost competitiveness.
candidates.next_evidence: Verify current offtake status, SK On and FCA termination disclosures, remaining Hiller Carbon or other agreements, financing runway, long-lead equipment orders, construction progress, qualification-line samples, and Phase I capex gap.
candidates.node_relation: Developer of the Kellyton Graphite Plant in Alabama, intended to process natural flake graphite into coated spherical purified graphite for lithium-ion battery anodes.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Battery-grade natural graphite processing and anode materials
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order exposure to non-Chinese graphite processing capacity, battery supply-chain localization, and critical-minerals policy support, but with severe financing and customer-risk flags.
candidates.why_include: Graphite processing is explicitly inside the node, and WWR is one of the few US-listed names attempting domestic battery-grade natural graphite processing. It is included only as a speculative exception because the market cap is below the preferred threshold.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is a micro-cap with messy financing status and customer churn; the chokepoint is real, but the company-specific survivability question may cause most institutional screens to exclude it.

evidence.claim: MP Materials entered definitive agreements with the US Department of Defense in July 2025 involving an end-to-end US rare-earth magnet supply chain, including DoD investment, a loan for heavy rare-earth separation, NdPr price-floor protection, and magnet offtake from the 10X facility.

The Department of Commerce CHIPS Program announced a letter of intent with USA Rare Earth to support its domestic vertically integrated mine-to-magnet strategy; the announcement referenced Round Top feedstock and a 2028 expected commercial production timeline.
evidence.source_title: The Department of Commerce’s CHIPS Program Announces a Letter of Intent with USA Rare Earth

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth reported Q1 2026 results and said the quarter included a $1.5 billion PIPE financing and an agreement for 100% economic consolidation of the Round Top project.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth’s investor-relations site states that the company commissioned a hydrometallurgical demonstration facility and is targeting heavy rare-earth oxide production in Q3 2026.

United States Antimony announced it was selected for a $27 million Defense Production Act Title III award to expand domestic extraction, processing, and refinement of critical materials, and described itself as the only domestic processor of antimony and producer of finished antimony products in the United States.
evidence.source_title: United States Antimony Corporation Selected for Strategic Antimony Supply Chain Expansion Under DoW Initiative

evidence.claim: United States Antimony’s 2025 Form 10-K says its principal business includes mining, procuring, processing and sale of antimony and precious metals, and that it acquired claims prospective for antimony, tungsten, cobalt, and other critical minerals.
evidence.source_title: United States Antimony Corporation Form 10-K for year ended December 31, 2025

evidence.claim: Westwater says the Kellyton Graphite Plant is being developed to process natural flake graphite into coated spherical purified graphite, the active anode material used in lithium-ion batteries.
evidence.source_title: Westwater Resources Operations - Kellyton Graphite Plant

evidence.claim: Westwater’s 2024 Form 10-K said the company reduced construction activity at Kellyton until receiving additional funding needed to complete Phase I, while also reporting then-existing offtake coverage for anticipated Phase I production.
evidence.source_title: Westwater Resources Form 10-K for year ended December 31, 2024

evidence.claim: Westwater later disclosed that SK On notified the company on March 31, 2026 of its decision to terminate the Products Procurement Agreement originally executed in February 2024.

memory_update.text: MP is the rare-earth reference anchor, not the underfollowed target; use it to benchmark policy support, price floors, heavy rare-earth separation, magnet offtake, and commissioning milestones.

USAR is an underfollowed mid-cap candidate for rare-earth processing and magnet-chain integration; survival depends on Round Top execution, hydrometallurgical performance, funding close, and customer qualification.

UAMY is a direct antimony-processing candidate with defense-policy tailwinds; later layers should verify actual throughput, contract economics, feedstock security, customer concentration, environmental compliance, and dilution risk.

WWR should remain a speculative_shadow graphite-processing exception because the node relevance is high but market cap, financing, and offtake durability are weak; require hard evidence before promotion.

Need a separate pass for US-listed or ADR-exposed gallium/germanium/tungsten recyclers, refiners, and equipment vendors; initial search surfaced private or non-US-listed assets such as Indium Corporation and Korea Zinc-linked projects, which are important supply-chain references but not clean US-listed candidates.

node: Critical minerals processing: heavy rare earths, graphite, gallium, germanium, antimony, tungsten, and magnet/refining capacity
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the critical-minerals-processing node with a two-lane structure: MP Materials as a high-attention reference anchor for rare-earth separation and magnets; USA Rare Earth and United States Antimony as more underfollowed pure-play processors/magnet or antimony-chain candidates; and Westwater Resources as a micro-cap speculative graphite-processing exception with high chokepoint relevance but major financing/customer-verification risk. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
